headline: Clean air and climate action returns $15 for every $1 spent
meta_description: A UN-backed report reveals coordinated action on air pollution and climate change can generate $15 in economic benefits per dollar invested while saving millio…
summary_short: A new UN report shows that tackling air pollution and climate change together can save millions of lives and generate $15 in economic returns for every $1 spent.
body:
A landmark UN-backed report has revealed that coordinated action on clean air and climate change can generate roughly $15 in economic benefits for every $1 invested, while simultaneously saving millions of lives and accelerating progress toward climate goals. Released on the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies on September 7, the assessment by the UN Environment Programme and the Climate and Clean Air Coalition demonstrates how 25 proven measures—from renewable energy and electric vehicles to clean cooking fuels and improved waste management—produce far higher returns when pursued together than when climate and air quality are addressed separately. By 2050, full implementation could prevent 144 million premature deaths linked to air pollution and reduce carbon dioxide emissions by half.

The economic case is striking. Annual benefits are projected to equal 2.8 percent of global GDP in 2035, rising to 4.5 percent by 2050. Even excluding non-market gains like added years of healthy life, the measures still return approximately $4 for every dollar spent. Yet the human toll of inaction remains severe: in 2025 alone, outdoor air pollution caused an estimated 6.4 million premature deaths worldwide, with household air pollution responsible for another two million deaths, including around 300,000 children.

Executive Director Inger Andersen emphasized the shift in perspective: "For too long, we have treated climate action as a cost to be managed and air pollution as the unfortunate outcome of development. This report shows the opposite: clean air is a key driver of development, health, food and energy security." The real challenge now lies in implementation. Fragmented decision-making and weak government coordination could delay full action by nearly eight years globally, making integrated planning and stronger institutions essential to unlock these proven benefits.
quick_facts: $15 in economic benefits returned per $1 invested in combined climate and air action
144 million air-pollution-related premature deaths could be prevented by 2050
6.4 million premature deaths linked to outdoor air pollution in 2025 alone
25 proven measures span energy, transport, industry, agriculture, cooking, and waste sectors
Report released September 7 by UN Environment Programme and Climate and Clean Air Coalition
